answer:
I found **34 papers** that report AlpacaEval win rates for their own model or method. To get there, I searched all 91 papers that mention AlpacaEval or AlpacaFarm and kept only those that score something they built themselves. Many papers mention AlpacaEval only in their references, related work or a survey table, and I dropped those.

**Foundation models and technical reports**
1. **Mixture-of-Agents**: their MoA reaches 65.8% LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0, against GPT-4o's 57.5% (p. 1–2).
2. **DeepSeek-V2**: the Chat model gets a 38.9 LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0 (p. 5); results table on p. 19.
3. **DeepSeek-V3**: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate in Table 7 (p. 33).
4. **DeepSeek-R1**: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate of 87.6 (p. 9); more tables on p. 41 and p. 56.
5. **OLMo**: AlpacaEval scores for the adapted OLMo models (p. 8, p. 21).
6. **2 OLMo 2 Furious**: AlpacaEval 2 (AE2) in the post-training results tables (p. 11, p. 28).
7. **Olmo 3**: AlpacaEval 2 LC (p. 7, p. 38–39, p. 54–55).
8. **Tülu 3**: AlpacaEval 2 LC % win (p. 6, p. 8–10).
9. **Nemotron-4 340B**: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC (p. 14).
10. **DataComp-LM**: the instruction-tuned DCLM model gets an AlpacaEval 2.0 LC win rate of 16.6 (p. 10); Table 26 on p. 72.

**Post-training data**
11. **AgentInstruct**: Orca-3 scores 24.80 on AlpacaEval, a 45% gain (p. 16; claim on p. 1, 3).
12. **HelpSteer2**: AlpacaEval 2.0 LC for their aligned models (p. 10–11).
13. **Magpie**: AlpacaEval 2 LC and win rate (p. 8–9; more on p. 18, 24–26).
14. **Self-Alignment with Instruction Backtranslation (Humpback)**: AlpacaEval win rate against text-davinci-003, Table 3 (p. 6).
15. **UltraFeedback**: win rate against text-davinci-003 on AlpacaEval (p. 5–6).
16. **WildFeedback**: AlpacaEval 2 rises from 24.3% to 42.6% (p. 8).
17. **WizardLM**: AlpacaEval column in the results tables (p. 7, p. 9, p. 22).

**Preference learning and RLHF**
18. **SimPO**: AlpacaEval 2 LC win rates, up to 6.4 points over DPO (p. 1–2).
19. **ORPO**: 12.20% on AlpacaEval 2.0 (p. 1); AlpacaEval 1.0 and 2.0 results (p. 5).
20. **KTO**: AlpacaEval (LC) in the table on p. 6; AlpacaEval 2 on p. 18.
21. **Self-Rewarding Language Models**: AlpacaEval 2.0 leaderboard results, Table 1 (p. 6).
22. **RLHF Workflow**: LC AlpacaEval-2 (p. 12); 37.2 LC / 45.4 raw win rate (p. 13).
23. **Unpacking DPO and PPO**: AlpacaEval 1 and 2; PPO beats DPO on AlpacaEval 2 by 3.4 points on average (p. 6).
24. **Generative Representational Instruction Tuning (GRIT)**: AlpacaEval jumps by more than 10 points with KTO (p. 7); ablations on p. 9–11.

**Other**
25. **Thinking LLMs (TPO)**: AlpacaEval LC win rates, Table 1 (p. 5) and Table 2 (p. 6).
26. **Checklists Are Better Than Reward Models (RLCF)**: AlpacaEval results (p. 7).
27. **Generalizing Verifiable Instruction Following**: their model scores 31.6 on AlpacaEval 2 (p. 20).
28. **Preference Leakage**: AlpacaEval 2.0 results for their trained student models, Table 1 (p. 5).
29. **Cheating Automatic LLM Benchmarks**: their "null model" gets an 86.5% LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0 (p. 1–2). Here the "method" is an adversarial cheat, not a real model.
30. **Privacy-Preserving Instructions**: AlpacaEval results for their SFT models (p. 8; Appendix D.6, p. 23).
31. **Safety Alignment Should Be Made More Than Just a Few Tokens Deep**: AlpacaEval 1.0 win rate (no length control) for their augmented model (p. 7, p. 16).
32. **FollowBench**: reports overall response quality using AlpacaEval (p. 8). My keyword search only showed this one line, so I haven't confirmed the scores are for their own model.

**Borderline**
33. **Length-Controlled AlpacaEval**: their contribution is the length-controlled metric itself. They show its win rates for leaderboard models and for gaming tests, e.g. 3.7 → 25.9 → 12.2 (p. 7).
34. **tinyBenchmarks**: estimates AlpacaEval 2.0 performance of existing models from fewer examples (p. 6–7). It reports no new model.

**Excluded, though they look close**
- **AlpacaFarm-style GPT-4 win rates, not AlpacaEval:** Back to Basics (p. 11), Personalized Soups (p. 6), Personalized Language Modeling from Personalized Human Feedback (p. 8), Preference Fine-Tuning … Suboptimal, On-Policy Data (p. 11, 27) and A Survey of LLMs (p. 88).
- **Towards Spec Learning:** uses the length-control method on its own datasets, not on the AlpacaEval benchmark (p. 17).
- **Qwen2.5-Omni:** reports a VoiceBench "AlpacaEval" score, not a win rate (p. 10).
- **Uses AlpacaEval data, but reports no win rates for a model of its own:** URIAL ("Unlocking Spell"), RewardBench, Inverse Constitutional AI, Trust or Escalate and AxBench.
